skill.name: pluto-pair
skill.description: Pair Codex with Pluto.jl notebooks through MCP tools for server discovery, live attachment, headless notebook execution, bond inspection, state reading, and HTML export.
skill.summary: Control and inspect Pluto.jl notebooks from Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through MCP tools.
skill.author: EzraCerpac

security_audit.summary: All static external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code spans around MCP tool names, not Ruby or shell execution. One contextual medium risk remains because the skill tells agents that opening a trusted Pluto notebook executes it by default, so users need clear trust and confirmation boundaries.

remediation.issue: Notebook execution is enabled by default for trusted notebooks.
remediation.suggestion: Document that agents should confirm notebook trust before execution and use disabled execution for unknown notebooks.

- `pluto_attach_session` to attach to a notebook already running in that visible server.
- `pluto_open_visible` to open a notebook in the visible server and attach to it.

- `pluto_set_bonds` to set bound values and trigger Pluto reactivity.
- `pluto_read_state` to summarize code, outputs, errors, logs, and bonds.
- `pluto_export_html` to write a rendered HTML export.

Line 12 is a Markdown bullet naming the pluto_discover_servers MCP tool. The backticks are documentation formatting, not command execution.
Line 13 is a Markdown bullet naming the pluto_attach_session MCP tool. No shell invocation or user-controlled command construction is present.
Line 14 is a Markdown bullet naming the pluto_open_visible MCP tool. The inline code span is descriptive text rather than executable Ruby or shell syntax.
Line 20 is a Markdown bullet naming the pluto_list_notebooks MCP tool. It does not contain code that would execute an external command.
Line 21 uses backticks to format a tool name and an option value in Markdown. The broader notebook execution behavior is contextual and is handled as a separate semantic finding.
Line 22 is Markdown documentation for the pluto_list_bonds tool and @bind variables. The backticks do not create a shell execution path.
Line 23 is a Markdown bullet naming the pluto_set_bonds MCP tool. It describes tool usage and contains no Ruby backtick execution.
Line 24 is a Markdown bullet naming the pluto_read_state MCP tool. The inline code span is not executable code.
Line 25 is a Markdown bullet naming the pluto_export_html MCP tool. It does not run a command or construct shell input.

semantic_findings.title: Default Notebook Execution Can Run Code
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md says pluto_open_notebook opens and executes a trusted notebook, with execution enabled by default. A community skill that drives notebook execution can run project code if trust boundaries are unclear.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Line 21 directly states notebooks are executed by default. Confidence is not higher because the same line limits this behavior to trusted notebooks and names a disabled execution mode for untrusted previews.

content.value_statement: Pluto.jl notebook work often needs live state, reactive controls, and rendered outputs. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code inspect, drive, and export notebooks through MCP tools.
actual_capabilities: Discover local Pluto servers and attach to visible notebook sessions.
Open Pluto notebooks in a visible server or a headless session.
Inspect @bind controls and set bond values to trigger reactive updates.
Read compact notebook state, including code, outputs, errors, logs, and bonds.
Detach from live sessions or close headless notebooks when work is complete.
limitations: Requires a configured pluto-pair MCP server and an accessible Pluto.jl environment.
Notebook execution can run Julia code, so unknown notebooks need disabled execution.
Does not replace manual review of notebook outputs or side effects.
Browser automation is limited to visual smoke checks and screenshots.

use_cases.title: Inspect a Live Notebook
use_cases.description: Attach to an open Pluto notebook, summarize its current state, and identify visible errors or controls.

use_cases.title: Test Reactive Parameters
use_cases.description: List @bind controls, set selected values, and compare resulting notebook outputs.

use_cases.title: Export Notebook Results
use_cases.description: Run a trusted notebook headlessly, check for errors, and export the rendered HTML.

prompt_templates.title: Attach to My Notebook
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Pluto Pair to discover local Pluto.jl servers, attach to my visible notebook if available, and summarize the current state.

prompt_templates.title: Review Interactive Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Pluto Pair to list @bind controls in the active notebook, explain their current values, and identify controls that affect the main output.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Trusted Notebook
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Pluto Pair to open this trusted notebook headlessly, run it, read compact state, report errors, and close the session when finished.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Parameter Sweep
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Pluto Pair to set these bond values across several runs, compare the resulting outputs, export the final HTML, and report any notebook errors.

output_examples.input: Inspect the open notebook and summarize controls.
output_examples.output: Attached to the visible Pluto notebook. It has three interactive controls, no current cell errors, and one warning in the logs.

output_examples.input: Run a trusted notebook headlessly and report problems.
output_examples.output: Opened the notebook in a headless session. Most cells completed, but one cell reported a missing package before the session was closed.

output_examples.input: Set the scenario selector to baseline and export HTML.
output_examples.output: Updated the bound control, waited for reactive updates, and exported the rendered notebook HTML.

best_practices: Confirm notebook trust before execution and use disabled execution for unknown notebooks.
Prefer live attach when the user already has a visible Pluto window.
Close or detach sessions after reading state or exporting results.
anti_patterns: Opening unknown notebooks with execution enabled.
Changing bond values without explaining the expected impact to the user.
Using browser automation when MCP notebook state tools provide the needed data.

faq.question: Does this skill execute notebooks?
faq.answer: Yes, when opening a trusted notebook with execution enabled. Use disabled execution for untrusted previews.

faq.question: Can it attach to a notebook I already opened?
faq.answer: Yes. It can discover visible Pluto servers and attach to a running notebook session.

faq.question: Can it change interactive controls?
faq.answer: Yes. It can inspect @bind variables and set bond values to trigger Pluto reactivity.

faq.question: Does it need a Pluto server?
faq.answer: Yes. It needs the pluto-pair MCP server and an accessible Pluto.jl environment.

faq.question: Can it export notebooks?
faq.answer: Yes. It can export a rendered Pluto notebook as HTML.

faq.question: Is it only for Codex?
faq.answer: No. It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when the MCP tools are available.
